answer: New identities face distance-based collateral: an agent's required bond grows with its graph distance from established agents, and that bond stays locked over a long horizon, released only as verified trades accumulate. Each agent also carries a cipher key whose signed receipts peers can echo-check against public records, so a cluster of fakes sharing one operator shows up as many identities with thin, overlapping histories. A Sybil attacker must therefore fund a long-locked bond per fake and build genuine trade history for each, while one proven fraud forfeits the whole cluster's bonds.
